newsitem.title: UK: Britain promises budget aid to Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Britain promises budget aid to Palestinians.

text.p: Britain said on Wednesday it had pledged $2 million to the Palestinian Authority following talks with planning minister Nabil Shaath.

"The aid is to help meet the Palestinian budgetary deficit which has worsened following recent Israeli border closures. Before the closures, budget performance for 1996 was btter than expected," the Overseas Development Administriation (ODA), Britain's official aid body, said in a statement.

It quoted Overseas Development Minister Baroness Chalker as reaffirming Britain's support for the Middle East peace process and promising to continue providing development assistance to the Palestinians.
Earlier this week, Shaath said his administration urgently needed an extra $20 million to cover a budget deficit this year.
He blamed the Israeli closure of borders for undermining the Palestinian economy and forcing it to depend on handouts from donors.

The amount pledged by Britain is below the $5 million Shaath wanted from each of four countries -- the others are Italy, Switzerland and Belgium -- he is currently visiting, accompanied by officials from the International Monetary Fund, World Bank and the United Nations.
An ODA spokesman said the $2 million was all the government had available. Since 1993 Britain has given around $55 million in aid to the Palestinians.
